scores.best_ideas: (1) The thesis sentence itself: "The zoom pulls back from a model on a table until the table is the world." That is images 1-2 said in the brief's own material: the same object (a model on a table) at every scale, and it is the only direction whose centre of gravity is the room with the oak table rather than the street or the instrument. (2) Each stage's accent IS its gate (Door gold, Letter Slot cyan, Clearinghouse gold, High Court's line paper, STARK ring cyan): the palette table encodes "state moves only at a boundary". (3) The thumbnail is the Door with its proof verbatim and a claim that can be checked in the frame: "One lit figure, one lit door, one sentence, provably true in the same frame: the gauge on the brass box has not moved since tick 1." Graft this sentence into whichever direction ships. (4) The dissolves as "a modeller's gesture": "1→2 roof and near wall fade in while translating down 0.6, the lid going back on; 2→3 the baseboard's bevelled --oak frame appears and the plinths rise 0 → 0.35". (5) "Waiting is stillness, not absence" and "a waiting figure has none" (no burn glow by rule). (6) "Bloom on gold: bloom is for cyan only, so a proof is the only thing that glows" is the cleanest bloom rule of the three. (7) "Ember is emissive, never a light." (8) Dust of 400 Points in L1's cone with alpha × (1 + fog): fog made physical without touching the truth shader. (9) The linen index-card HUD, and "The Note is a --paper card projected onto the Oak Table while node.note !== null". (10) §12's last bullet, "the DOM test that scans every frame for the brief's forbidden words is the first acceptance", is the right order of work.
scores.fatal_flaws: None fatal. Three things to fix before build: (a) Tilt-shift is a second blur competing with fog = 1 − Φ. A house soft because it is off the focus plane and a house soft because Φ is 0.56 will read the same to a viewer; make tilt-shift band-1 only or a quality option, never the default at Stage 2-3. (b) Only "Golden" and "Night" presets and a single "low" quality switch: the brief asked for the day/night and quality presets from mood 3; graft Colony's five lighting presets and Potato-to-Ultra ladder. (c) The Door card omits the "Recorded run · the person's answer replays at the recorded tick" line and the "sent to the Door…" non-optimistic state that the trace acceptance test needs; take both from Colony. Minor: 0.60 m figures at 46 px with flatShading and no outline will not truly be "legible at 16 px" without Colony's 1 px --oak-dark toon outline; the south-facing house on a ring kerb does not face the kerb for half the ring (Colony's cottage "whose long face looks at the kerb" is the fix).

scores.best_ideas: (1) The accent as a tense, not a colour: "Gold seals a commit, ember scars a loss. Gold leaf appears only after APPROVED/SETTLED; ember only for sunk_compute, SLASHED, HALTED. Before a gate decides, an envelope is plain paper." This is the sharpest colour rule in the set and should be grafted wholesale. (2) "Bottom edge, the root ticker: root_history as 16 engraved tabs, 8 hex each, newest right; a cyan tab on each GLOBAL_STATE_CONFIRMED", which makes ROLLED_BACK legible as "the ticker rewinds one tab to to_tick". (3) "SLASHED: ember flash 400 ms, the purse arc drops, a scorch mark stays until compute next changes": a visible memory of an event whose lifetime is keyed to a state field, not a timer. (4) The thumbnail's insight that decay and the held purse are two clocks in one frame: "one number that has not moved, while the hatching says time is passing anyway". (5) The argument that the STATE_SYNC band should be cyan ("sweepLight in vec3(0.16, 0.65, 0.72) (cyan, not gold)") because paying the oracle is verification; the map made it gold, and the Ledger's reason is better. (6) "Textures and normal maps: ... flat colour + line + hatch keeps 5,000 tiles in one draw call" is good perf discipline whichever look wins. (7) "Foundry and data-centre numbers. The engine has no such nodes, so they show no value."
scores.fatal_flaws: Two, and together they are the closest thing to fatal in the set. (a) Stage 4 becomes "a vellum page" at #a8967a, a light plate between a dark City (#2a2015) and a dark World (#0a0806). That is a luminance cut in the middle of the zoom, and the brief's one rule for the zoom is "continuous, self-similar, never a hard cut". The material changes per stage (brass plate → vellum page → brass sphere) instead of one rule at every scale. (b) The hatch is anchored to the screen: "vec2 p = gl_FragCoord.xy / 6.0". Under a continuously moving altitude camera, screen-space lines slide over the geometry (the shower-door effect), and 1 px lines at 6 px pitch alias and shimmer at 320 × 180 and under YouTube compression, which is the recording deliverable. It also replaces the brief's and doc 02's fog spec ("Perlin/simplex distortion increasing with fog") and the converged applyFog rather than extending it; the reason is written down, but it discards the shader three proposals converged on. Lesser: the world is brass, paper and ink with little oak, and the top-right "barometer" dial with two needles is the nearest thing to a rating instrument on any of the three screens; it shows only purse and Φ, so it passes the test, but a needle invites comparison. The HUD is the busiest (index tabs, brass strip, barometer, rotated receipt strip, footing with double rule, ticker), and the north-facing Door does not face the kerb on a ring.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The most complete Door dialog spec: Escape and backdrop cancelled, focus on No, "a click shows 'sent to the Door…', nothing optimistic", the recorded-run line, "1 of 2 at the Door", and the closing rule "only on the engine's APPROVED/REJECTED or a frame whose held no longer lists the envelope". Graft it verbatim. (2) The lighting ladder and quality ladder, which are exactly what the brief said to take from mood 3: five presets from Dawn to Night with "lanterns come up as the key light goes down", and "Potato (DPR 1, no shadows or bloom, one noise octave, ≤ 256 courier quads) … Ultra", plus "At most four point lights at once, so Potato still runs." (3) "Cycle day/night steps one preset every 64 ticks on TICK_COMMITTED, never wall time." (4) The house lantern as the status pill made physical: "gold steady active, cyan breathing waiting_at_door, ember halted, off when packed or partitioned", which matches the map's statusTint rim exactly. (5) The cottage "whose long face looks at the kerb" (the other two leave houses facing a fixed compass point on a ring). (6) "At 1↔2 nothing is composited: the roof lowers onto the room like a lid and the neighbours light their lanterns out of their own fog." (7) The pending-zoom rule said plainly: "the dissolve weight is clamped at 0.5 until PACKED/UNPACKED or a confirming TICK_COMMITTED arrives, so the camera never shows a scale the engine is not simulating." (8) The thumbnail's composition reasoning: "one gold rectangle (the boundary), one white rectangle (the thing that wants to cross it), and a cat between them" and the 320 × 180 check. (9) "Lanterns hang on boundaries, never in interiors" is a good fractal rule: one object at every gate at every scale.
scores.fatal_flaws: Not fatal to the direction, but two things must go. (a) The hero frame demotes the Door. The thumbnail rewrites the brief's sentence to "Nothing burns while we wait." and shows "No HUD but the block line", so the proof (Held N · purse unchanged · Φ then, now) is absent from the one frame the video leads with. "You decide" is the moral point: the person's act, not the helpers' patience. The Colony's own dialog spec has the right words; its thumbnail chose the street over the Door. (b) The Stage 3 street rim invents a value not in any frame: "--sage when its last SETTLED was within 16 ticks, --gold-2 otherwise". A 16-tick recency window is frontend arithmetic, and a rim that says "this street was busy lately" is the first step toward the board the brief bans; the Diorama's §12 refuses exactly this ("any number not in a frame"). Lesser: the opening line, "The hex-colony frame's joy … rebuilt in the room's materials", says the quiet part: this is the reference re-skinned, with the settings rail imported as "the mood frame's settings column in oak", where the brief said the room is the target world and the frame is mood only; glaze, terracotta and lantern glass are a village material family the brief never named; "Bloom … touches cyan and lantern glass, never gold" is hair-splitting when lantern glass is #f6d89a and --gold-light is #f2cb7a, and by its own words "it turns brass into neon"; gold is overloaded (the human hand, the brass that waits, active, and not-recently-settled); the HUD has seven zones. The "About 32 px at the room's default altitude" figure is wrong (0.9 m at H = 14 m on 1080 rows is ~69 px), harmless but a sign the numbers were not all checked.

judge:director.rationale:
The brief's centre is one sentence, "state moves only at a boundary, and nothing is shared by default", and its target world is "the room with the oak table". The Diorama is the only direction whose world is that room, scaled: "room, street and city are one architectural model under warm lamps" and "the zoom pulls back from a model on a table until the table is the world." That is images 1-2 (the same rule at every zoom) said in the room's own material, and its dissolves are the modeller's hands on the model (the lid going back on, the baseboard appearing, the plate becoming a plateau, the relief settling onto the globe) rather than a render-target trick. Its palette encodes the thesis: each stage's accent is that stage's gate. Its thumbnail is the Door as the brief wrote it, with the live proof, and adds a claim that can be verified in the frame ("the gauge on the brass box has not moved since tick 1"). It keeps the converged truth shader untouched (lowest risk of the three), and it names the forbidden-word DOM test as "the first acceptance". It takes from mood 3 what the ruling allowed (dimetric hex zoning, readable actors, depth, presets) and nothing of its kit.

The Colony is the runner-up and the most buildable: the most complete Door dialog, the best lighting and quality ladders, the cottage that turns to face the kerb, and the honest pending-zoom clamp. But it is, by its own first line, the mood frame "rebuilt in the room's materials", and its hero frame rewrites the Door's line to "while we wait" and drops the proof, which demotes the moral centre to set-dressing in the one frame that matters. Its 16-tick street-rim recency invents a value no frame carries. Those are grafts to make and lines to cut, not reasons to build it as the base.

The Ledger has the best single colour rule ("Before a gate decides, an envelope is plain paper") and the best small mechanisms (the root ticker tabs, the scorch that lasts until compute changes, the cyan sweep argument), but the vellum page at Stage 4 is a hard luminance cut in a zoom that must never cut, and screen-space hatching swims under a moving camera and dies under video compression. It is also the least oak and the least joy.

Build the Diorama. Graft into it: Colony's dialog spec (recorded-run line, "sent to the Door…", cancel rules), Colony's five lighting presets and Potato-to-Ultra ladder with the four-point-light cap, Colony's kerb-facing cottage and lantern-as-status-pill, Colony's 1 px toon outline on the figures; Ledger's plain-paper-until-decided rule, its root ticker, its SLASHED scorch keyed to compute, and its case for a cyan STATE_SYNC band. Cut from the Diorama: tilt-shift as a default above band 1 (it fights fog = 1 − Φ). None of the three touches hosting; all consume the same EngineSource (wasm, SSE, trace), so the Cloud Run material in the main repo does not change the ranking.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The zoom as a modeller's gesture: "1→2 roof and near wall fade in while translating down 0.6, the lid going back on; 2→3 the baseboard's bevelled --oak frame appears and the plinths rise 0 → 0.35 as the outgoing band fogs out; 3→4 the city plate becomes one plateau of the relief; 4→5 the relief fades onto the globe" — the fractal thesis as a camera move, and the best YouTube shot of the three. (2) The whole NETTED choreography "four beats from one uPulses entry" — one uniform write per event, zero CPU per frame, exactly the map's pulse ring. (3) The purity statement is the crispest: "otherwise only dust, lamps and the fog's breath move, on uTime" and "values that change without an event are block-lerped between two engine truths"; plus "the DOM test that scans every frame for the brief's forbidden words is the first acceptance". (4) The Door card's live-proof rule ("purse unchanged at X cr while node.compute === openedAt.compute, else purse X cr → Y cr (topped up)"; "closes only when state.held no longer lists the envelope") and a thumbnail that trace.json reproduces to the digit (tick 4: Held 3, 754.95, 97.3% → 89.3%). (5) "Set dressing reads no truth (aSlot = −1)" and "Shadow maps above band 2 [left out]: a lit side face and a baked contact shadow read the same at 5,000 plinths" — the right performance instinct at scale. (6) The packed street as "one smooth cast block (aFold = 1), #3e3a34 resin ... the Mandelbrot interior, nothing moving inside" is the best stasis image. (7) Bloom "for cyan only, so a proof is the only thing that glows".
scores.fatal_flaws: (1) The signature transition does not line up as written: §4 puts the Door on the east wall ("D Door, z -0.5..0.5" at x = +4, "The Porter stops 0.5 m short of x = 4.0") while §6 puts "The Letter Slot ... on the south-face Door" with the house "1.2 from the south (kerb) edge". The 1↔2 "lid going back on" needs the room and the cottage to share one Door; agents B (tiles) and C (room) would build two. Must be reconciled before day 0. (2) The heaviest render path of the three: tilt-shift ("a half-resolution two-pass blur masked by |depth − focusDepth|" = a depth RT plus two passes), two shadow maps ("shadows 1024²" spot and "shadows 2048²" directional), selective bloom on cyan, 400 dust Points, morph-target figures, and PBR brass "metalness 0.85 roughness 0.35" which renders near-black under punctual lights without an environment map (needs RoomEnvironment + PMREM; slow on SwiftShader, and every pass is another golden-screenshot surface). At band 3 with the tilt-shift on, 60 fps on Iris Xe at DPR 1.5 is at risk; on M1 it is fine. Each piece is standard three.js, but together they overload agent C for a one-session build. (3) L2 goes "0 → 1.4 on AWAITING_HUMAN_SIGNATURE" and nothing turns it off or on from state; a trace replay started mid-hold shows an open Door and a dark lamp. Trivial fix (read held > 0), but it is the one place the direction animates from an event without a state fallback. (4) `--brass #a8842e` sits within a few units of the brief's gold marks `#b98626`; "gold is the human hand and the brass that waits for it" merges them on purpose, which blurs 'gold = a commit' at Stage 3 where the dome is brass and the pulse is gold. (5) Only two lighting presets and no named quality ladder beyond "off on low"; the brief asked to take the mood reference's presets.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The accent grammar is the thesis as colour: "Gold seals a commit, ember scars a loss. Gold leaf appears only after APPROVED/SETTLED; ember only for sunk_compute, SLASHED, HALTED. Before a gate decides, an envelope is plain paper." Nothing else in the three directions encodes 'state moves only at a boundary' this literally. (2) Hatch-as-fog: "Fog is drawn, never simulated. Hatch density is 1 − Φ" with a 15-line applyHatch that replaces the map's simplex warp + grain + chroma split with one snoise call and four stripe() evaluations — cheaper per fragment, deterministic under page.clock, and it reads as engraving rather than JPEG damage; four visible density grades map Φ legibly. (3) The leanest render path of the three, stated as policy: "flat colour + line + hatch keeps 5,000 tiles in one draw call"; "Dynamic shadows beyond the pendant [left out]. Hatching is the shadow"; "Bloom on gold, and any bloom in the room [left out]". This is the direction I can ship on SwiftShader goldens without a fight. (4) "A receipt is an object": node.receipts verbatim on the receipt strip, and the root ticker "root_history as 16 engraved tabs, 8 hex each, newest right; a cyan tab on each GLOBAL_STATE_CONFIRMED" — root_history is in StateView and nobody else draws it. (5) The barometer focus card ("gold needle = compute / compute_allocated, cyan needle = confidence, ember arc under 15 %") is a single instrument the eye learns in one look. (6) The Door card is complete to the brief, including "Recorded run · the person's answer replays at the recorded tick", and TICK_COMMITTED has an explicit 0 ms row. (7) The dissolve as "the loupe moving across one plate" (outgoing band hatched to full, incoming un-hatched outward from the focus) reuses the map's half-res RT with the hatch as the medium.
scores.fatal_flaws: (1) The thumbnail contradicts its own shader: "the room carries a thin single-direction hatch (Φ 0.893)" but `stripe(p, 0.0) * smoothstep(0.15, 0.25, fog)` is 0 at fog 0.107; the first hatch only appears below Φ 0.85, so at the Door (Φ 0.973 → 0.893 over ticks 1–4) the plate is clean and "the hatching says time is passing anyway" is false. Fix: first threshold smoothstep(0.02, 0.12, fog). One constant, but it is the thesis frame. (2) The motion table misses DROPPED_BY_COURIER entirely (not in the text at all) and AWAITING_FINALITY as a row (only §8 prose); the brief's Stage 2 courier list needs the drop, and clips.test.ts wants all 22 variants named. (3) "Night `#7c88a8` ×0.35" is a blue key light: at night the whole plate goes cold, against its own principle "One cold colour exists and it means 'verified'"; the "cyan needle = confidence" likewise spends cyan on a value rather than a verification event. (4) Two value-triggered rules: "a scorch mark stays until compute next changes" and "The proof line is recomputed each frame while open" — clear the scorch on TOPPED_UP/TICK_COMMITTED and patch the proof in reduce(), not per render frame. (5) Small implementation traps: "inverted-hull ink outline" cracks at the hard edges of a flat-shaded 12-facet body unless the hull copy carries smoothed normals; "Hatch pitch scales with uAltitude to stay 6 px on screen" is redundant with `gl_FragCoord.xy / 6.0` (already screen-space) and needs `/ (6.0 * DPR)`; screen-space hatch swims under camera motion (accept as the engraving's nature, or anchor to tile UV at bands 1–2); "cities are brass studs ... on the ridges" conflicts with "a seeded heightfield (world-space simplex)" because layoutCountry is a ring layout — compose the heightfield around the city cells; `--paper-ink` is not a defined token. (6) It takes the least of the mood reference's joy: "Porter idle until the Audit paper lands", no bustle, the busiest HUD (eight zones).

scores.best_ideas: (1) The only motion table covering all 22 EngineEvent variants, with absolute NETTED beats ("(1) 0–240 ms, every tube fills inward ... (2) 240–400 ms, the dome flares --gold ... (3) from 400 ms, one thin ring leaves the dome outward at 40 ms per hex, width scaled by net / gross, tinted --sage") — clips.ts can be typed straight from it. (2) The best DOM discipline: "patched in reduce() and on clip boundaries, never per render frame" and "a click shows 'sent to the Door…', nothing optimistic". (3) Concrete performance rules: "At most four point lights at once, so Potato still runs"; "octaves 3 in the room, 2 on the street, 1 above"; "Cycle day/night steps one preset every 64 ticks on TICK_COMMITTED, never wall time". (4) Lantern-as-status gives per-house legibility at 5,000 tiles without a label: "gold steady active ... ember halted, off when packed or partitioned", and street rims "--sage when its last SETTLED was within 16 ticks, --gold-2 otherwise, --ember while any house on it is halted, off when packed". (5) Stasis stated exactly: "The children's cells are unlit --glaze plates with the roof on and no lantern; nothing moves on them, because their clocks are stopped." (6) Five lighting presets where "lanterns come up as the key light goes down" — the mood reference's slider rebuilt in oak and brass, as the brief asked. (7) Zoom confirmation: "the dissolve weight is clamped at 0.5 until PACKED/UNPACKED or a confirming TICK_COMMITTED arrives, so the camera never shows a scale the engine is not simulating".
scores.fatal_flaws: (1) The thumbnail drops the brief's sentence and its evidence: "Over the Door, one DOM pill: 'Nothing burns while we wait.'" (the vocabulary is "Nothing burns while you decide") and "No HUD but the block line", so the live proof (Held N · purse unchanged · Φ then/now) is off the thesis frame. It also runs at "altitude 1.3 ... the roof is lifting" while its own dissolve window is [1.35, 1.65]. (2) It contradicts its own palette rule two paragraphs apart: "Cyan is verification only" and then "The lantern says the status: ... cyan breathing waiting_at_door" (inherited from the map's statusTint, but written into the direction; waiting should be the gold desk lamp, as Diorama and Ledger do). (3) "Four clips per cat on a six-bone rig" plus hand-cart couriers as the same rig is the single most expensive art task in all three directions when authored in code in one session; Diorama's five morph targets or a transform-pose kit costs a fifth of it. (4) Surface area: five quality presets ("Potato ... Ultra (DPR ≤ 2, 2048 shadow map, particles ×2)"), a six-control settings rail, a zoom rail, a feed drawer, lantern posts every three cells, foundries with plumes, longhouses — each is a code path and a SwiftShader golden; it is the mood frame's rail rebuilt, but not a one-session build. (5) Arithmetic and geometry looseness: "hex prisms (36 indices" is the sides only (a capped prism is 48); "About 32 px at the room's default altitude" is wrong at H = 14 m (0.90 m ≈ 69 px at 1080p; Diorama's 0.60 m → 46 px is right); "a pointy-top hex ... the porch on the tile's eastern point" — a pointy-top hex has no eastern point. (6) "APPROVED: Door swings 30°" barely reads at fov 4° dimetric; Diorama's 70° does. (7) "within 16 ticks" is a frontend-invented window (allowed, since it is derived from events and never printed, but it is a number not in any frame).

judge:engineer.rationale: All three directions stand on the converged map (one InstancedMesh, the RGBA16F truth texture, uTruthPrev block lerp, the reducer-written STATE_SYNC cascade, uPulses, the altitude camera with hysteresis), so 5,000 tiles at 60 fps is an architecture property in each; the judgment is about what each stacks on the tile pass and whether one session with five parallel agents can finish it and prove it on SwiftShader. On those two criteria the Ledger is clearly ahead: no shadow maps beyond one pendant, no bloom in the room, no post blur, no PBR environment, no rig, and a fog that is four stripe() calls and one snoise instead of three-octave domain-warped simplex with a chroma re-sample. Its flaws are constants and table rows (the hatch threshold that hides Φ 0.893, the missing DROPPED_BY_COURIER and AWAITING_FINALITY rows, the cold night key, the cyan Φ needle, `--paper-ink`), each a ten-minute fix. The Diorama ties it on paper and beats it on delight, but its flaws are structural: the Door is on the east wall in §4 and the south face in §6, which breaks the "lid going back on" transition that is its best idea, and its render stack (tilt-shift depth pass + two blur passes, two shadow maps, selective bloom, PMREM brass, dust, morph figures) is a third more passes than the brief's laptop target and the SwiftShader golden suite can absorb in one session. The Colony is the most complete spec (the only 22-row table, the best reduce()-only DOM rule) but it rewrites the brief's sentence in its own thumbnail, hides the proof line, contradicts its own cyan rule, and asks for a six-bone skinned rig and five quality presets; it is the right list of features for a second session. The Ledger also carries the thesis best in colour: "Before a gate decides, an envelope is plain paper" and gold leaf only after APPROVED/SETTLED is 'state moves only at a boundary' made visible, and its thumbnail is reproducible from trace.json to the digit (tick 4: Held 3, 754.95 cr, 97.3% → 89.3%). Build the Ledger and graft: from the Diorama, the NETTED four beats from one uPulses entry, the sage rim ticks on tiles that SETTLED as beat four, the packed street as one smooth resin block, L2 and the Door frame read from `held > 0`, and its two lighting presets (Golden, Night with a warm `#8a7a64` key so cyan stays the only cold colour) in place of the Ledger's five; from the Colony, the 22-row table as the clips.ts source, "patched in reduce() and on clip boundaries, never per render frame", "sent to the Door…" as the click state, the four-point-light cap, octaves by band, the TICK_COMMITTED-driven day cycle, and the lantern-as-status at Stages 2–3 recoloured to the Ledger's grammar (gold lit active, lamp-and-frame waiting, ember halted, off packed). Before day 0 for whoever builds it: lower the first hatch threshold to smoothstep(0.02, 0.12, fog), divide the hatch pitch by DPR, give the inverted hull smoothed normals, compose the country heightfield around the city cells, and note that the shared `smoothstep(0.75, 0.55, phi)` (reversed edges, in the map's applyFog and the Ledger's applyHatch alike) is undefined per the GLSL spec and should be written as `1.0 - smoothstep(0.55, 0.75, phi)` so SwiftShader and ANGLE agree.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The nested-model zoom is the best answer of the three to the mood-1/2 'same rule at every zoom' ruling: '1→2 roof and near wall fade in while translating down 0.6, the lid going back on; 2→3 the baseboard's bevelled --oak frame appears and the plinths rise 0 → 0.35; 3→4 the city plate becomes one plateau of the relief; 4→5 the relief fades onto the globe.' Graft this dissolve grammar wholesale. (2) 'Bloom is for cyan only, so a proof is the only thing that glows.' (3) The thumbnail's light hierarchy: 'L1 pools gold on the Oak Table's east end … The Porter is at the step, envelope out, still, throwing a long shadow toward the Archives' — one lamp pool, one long shadow, one lit door is the correct recipe for a 320×180 read. (4) Principle 4, 'A miniature never lies about scale: one camera, one altitude, one lamp rig' — the Colony needs exactly this rule. (5) The Door 'swings 70°' (a yes you can see from across the room), the DOM scan 'for the brief's forbidden words is the first acceptance', and the globe 'on a brass stand' with the armillary ring as the STARK track. (6) Principle 5, 'Waiting is stillness, not absence … a boundary that holds is the thesis.'
scores.fatal_flaws: Small-screen legibility. It stacks tilt-shift ('the model's edges blur'), '400 Points' of dust, quadratic grain and a chroma split onto a #19130d/#2c2219 warm-dark room, with the smallest actors of the three (0.60 m: 46 px at 1080p, ~8 px in a 320×180 thumbnail). YouTube's compressor turns dark blur plus grain into blocks; on a phone this is brown mush with one bright rectangle, and the thumbnail then leans on a sentence on a linen card ('Nothing burns while you decide. Held 3 ticks…') that no one can read at that size. For a colour-vision-deficient viewer the Φ channel is desaturation ('desaturates toward the tint') and blur — the two things I already see less of. Second, brass is everywhere ('hardware: Door frame, dome, desk lamp', kerb studs, tube saddles, the armillary ring) and #a8842e sits next to gold #b98626, so 'gold is the human hand' is diluted; and its own colour rule breaks: 'sage is settled or approved' yet APPROVED plays gold. Third, it violates its own principle 4 between stages: the room's Door is on the east wall (x = 4.0) but the street house has 'the south-face Door', so 'the lid going back on' cannot be frame-consistent. Fourth, joy: 'carved figures do not emote', interiors are still, motion budget only on rims — the Director asked for the colony's joy and this is museum hush. Not fatal to shipping, but fatal to the thesis reading on a phone.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The single best idea across all three, and the one that makes 'gate decides, then the world changes' visible without reading: 'Before a gate decides, an envelope is plain paper' and 'Gold seals a commit, ember scars a loss. Gold leaf appears only after APPROVED/SETTLED.' A gate's yes becomes a material change on the object. Graft into the winner unchanged. (2) Fog as hatching (`applyHatch`): a pattern channel, not a hue channel, so a colour-vision-deficient viewer reads Φ exactly as everyone else; and the STATE_SYNC front 'erases lines as it passes' is the most legible clearing of the three. Keep it at least as the reduced-motion / accessibility fog mode. (3) 'Engrave the boundary, ink the interior … cut deepest and lit brightest, because state moves only there' — luminance carries the thesis, which is the right channel for CVD and for thumbnails. (4) 'A receipt is an object': slips that drop 'to the drawer' under the Desk, 'a scorch mark stays until compute next changes', 'a gold leaf seal stamps the kerb' — the story's 'piece of paper that lets you see the burn', drawn. (5) 'Inverted-hull ink outline 1 px in --oak-dark' on the cats: the cheapest, best small-size separation of figure from ground. (6) Geometry honesty: the room's Door at 'x 6.6–7.4' on the north wall is the same Door on the street house's 'north face at x 6.6–7.4' — the only direction whose 1↔2 dissolve can be true frame for frame. (7) Cheapest render: 'flat colour + line + hatch keeps 5,000 tiles in one draw call', one shadow map, no textures.
scores.fatal_flaws: Contrast on a phone. At rest the world is two dark browns (--plate #2a2015 under --engrave #6b5330) with --hatch #0e0a06 laid over; only lines that 'catch the key light' via Fresnel brighten. In daylight on a phone the boundaries vanish and the frame is a brown page; the 6 px hatch will moiré and shimmer under YouTube compression and collapses to flat tone at 180p. Second, the zoom breaks its own continuity: Stage 4 becomes a 'vellum page #a8967a', a light page between a dark city and a dark brass globe — a tonal hard cut inside a zoom the brief says must be 'continuous, self-similar, never a hard cut'. Third, HUD weight: a 180 px two-needle 'barometer' (to a first-time viewer a dial with a needle reads as a rating, the one affordance the brief bans in spirit), a 'root ticker … 16 engraved tabs, 8 hex each', the 'receipt strip' plus 'the 40-line event feed' — the heaviest text load of the three, unreadable on a phone and noise in a thumbnail. Fourth, joy: 'The viewer reads a barometer of the economy'; cats get 'two ink dots' for a face; interiors are 'flat plate with quiet hatching'. It is an instrument, not a place, and the ruling explicitly asked for the colony's joy. Small: 'Cyan is spent only on verification … the Inspector's stamp', yet the stamp is 'sage tick or ember mark'.

scores.best_ideas: (1) The thumbnail is the only one of the three that shows all four beats of the thesis in one frame with no words: 'the house tile fills the left two-thirds: the roof is lifting, the room is open, four cats are frozen at their stations, and the Porter stands at the Door with a white envelope held out … Through the open east wall the kerb runs off to the right, where three neighbouring cottages sit dim in their own fog with one brass letter slot each catching lantern light.' Private drafting, the envelope, the gate, and a world outside that has not changed yet: 'many houses, one door open'. (2) Lanterns as status with a behaviour channel, not just a hue: 'gold steady active, … breathing waiting_at_door, ember halted, off when packed or partitioned' — steady/breathing/off reads for a colour-vision-deficient viewer. (3) 'Lanterns come up as the key light goes down' and 'Cycle day/night steps one preset every 64 ticks on TICK_COMMITTED, never wall time' — the mood frame's presets kept on-palette and on the engine's word. (4) Engine-word discipline at the Door: 'a click shows "sent to the Door…", nothing optimistic'; the dialog 'closes only on the engine's APPROVED/REJECTED'; the recorded-run line is present. (5) The crispness the ruling asked for: --glaze/--glaze-lit bevels, --terracotta roofs, 1 px toon outlines, contact shadows — three tonal tiers instead of one dark. (6) Stage 3: the dome 'itself a lantern', per-street rim lanterns, and the NETTED ring 'tinted --sage, so a heavily netted city visibly sends less out than came in'. (7) 'SEAT_FAILED: the seat's chair tips and rights itself' — the small joy the others lack.
scores.fatal_flaws: None fatal; four to fix before build. (1) The 'cyan breathing waiting_at_door' lantern contradicts its own rule ('Cyan is verification only') and the shared vocabulary (waiting is the human hand, gold): at Stage 2 a first-time viewer reads a held house as 'being verified'. Make it gold breathing. (2) Scale drift 1→2: the room is '8 m east–west by 6 m north–south' with the Door on 'the east wall x = 4.0', but the street cottage is '6 × 5 × 4.5 m' with the door 'centred on the kerb face' of its long side — so 'the roof lowers onto the room like a lid' is not frame-true. Adopt Diorama's principle 4 and Ledger's matching coordinates. (3) Overclaim: 'At 320 × 180 the hex, the door and the envelope are still three distinct shapes' — a 0.24 m envelope in a 14 m view is 3 px, a bright dot; shoot the thumbnail at a lower altitude or crop. (4) Wording drift: the thumbnail pill says 'Nothing burns while we wait' where the brief mandates 'Nothing burns while you decide'. The real risk is distinctiveness: it is the mood frame in oak and, on its own, could read as a generic cosy isometric village (and 'bloom … lantern glass' dilutes 'a proof is the only thing that glows'). Without Ledger's plain-paper-to-gold-leaf rule and Diorama's nested-model dissolves it is pleasant rather than memorable.

judge:viewer.rationale:
Judged as a first-time YouTube viewer and as a colour-vision-deficient viewer, on the four beats of the thesis with no captions. Only the Colony's thumbnail shows all four in one frame: an open room with staff at the Oak Table (private drafting), the Porter's white envelope at a gold-framed Door (the envelope, the gate), and three dim neighbours with unlit Letter Slots beyond the kerb (a world that has not changed yet). The Diorama's frame is the room alone and depends on a sentence on a linen card; the Ledger's is a plate, a paper and a dial. On a phone and at 320×180, the Colony has the most tonal range (terracotta roofs, glaze bevels, lantern glass over dark ground) and crisp outlined edges; the Diorama blurs its own edges and adds dust and grain to a dark room, which YouTube compression turns to blocks; the Ledger at rest is two dark browns under hatching. For a CVD viewer the Ledger is structurally the best (Φ as pattern, boundaries as the brightest lines, gold only after a commit) and the Colony is second but easily fixed by grafting; the Diorama is the worst because its Φ channel is desaturation and blur, which such a viewer already experiences. On joy, the only direction that answers the Director's ruling ('take from it … the readable little actors going about their work … the joy') is the Colony: bustling cats, lanterns coming up as the sun goes down, a chair that tips on SEAT_FAILED. The Diorama is museum hush ('carved figures do not emote'); the Ledger is a barometer. All three are shippable on a laptop; the Ledger is cheapest, the Colony middling, the Diorama heaviest (two shadow maps plus a tilt-shift pass plus a warped fog shader at band 1). Totals: Colony 34, Ledger 31, Diorama 29.

Build the Colony with these grafts, in this order: (1) Ledger's colour law — an envelope is plain --paper until the gate says yes, gold leaf only after APPROVED/SETTLED, ember only for sunk cost — so the gate's decision is a visible change of material on the object itself; (2) Diorama's nested-model dissolve grammar (the lid at 1→2, the bevelled oak baseboard appearing at 2→3, the plate becoming a plateau at 3→4, the relief fading onto the globe at 4→5), which also gives the zoom the fractal continuity the brief asks for; (3) Ledger's `applyHatch` as the reduced-motion and accessibility fog, and as the hatch-erasing form of the STATE_SYNC sweep, blended under the lantern smoke at the default quality; (4) Ledger's 1 px inverted-hull ink outline on the cats; (5) Diorama's 'bloom on cyan only' — drop bloom on lantern glass so a proof is the only thing that glows; (6) Diorama's principle 4 and Ledger's matching room/street coordinates to fix the Colony's 8×6 to 6×5 footprint and door jump; (7) change the waiting lantern from cyan to gold breathing and restore the brief's sentence 'Nothing burns while you decide' everywhere it appears; (8) Diorama's DOM forbidden-word scan as the first acceptance test. Keep the Colony's HUD but cap it on phones to the block line, the focus card and the Door; leave the Ledger's root ticker, receipt strip and barometer out. The verbatim user note about Google Cloud Run in the main repo does not bear on this scoring and was not acted on.
